subject: LatticeWorks peak-slope analysis and GPU buffer recommendation
summary: Decision note and recommendation for Dedicated GPU slab sizing for LatticeWorks deal. We model token/sec demand curves, SLO fit, and recommend a safety buffer and concrete GPU counts for model variants and burst scenarios.
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sam Todd <sam.todd@latticeworks.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LatticeWorks — quick ask: real peak slope + latency SLOs

Sam — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I sketched a quick capacity exercise to map your projected traffic to a Dedicated slab recommendation. Before we lock numbers we need two clarifications from your side so our sizing is defensible: 

1) Traffic shape: you gave a daily peak window (09:00–11:00 PT) but we need the "peak slope" — how quickly traffic moves from baseline to peak. Specifically: baseline RPS and peak RPS at 5, 10, and 30 minute roll-ups. If you only have hourly, tell us the max hourly concurrency and we'll conservatively model a 5x concentrated peak.
2) Latency SLO: you mentioned 95th percentile generation latency target of 350ms for shortest prompts and "sub-second" for average flows. Please confirm the 95th-pct SLO (ms) and whether you accept fallback to an 8-bit quantized model under heavy burst.

Attached: LW-2345_token_profile.xlsx (sheet with our throughput-to-GPU mapping assumptions) and an early PDF with buffer math.

If you can reply with the two items above today, Ben and Karthik will run a rapid slab simulation (incl. burst buffer suggestions) and propose a firm Dedicated commit.

Thanks —
Stephanie
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

From: Sam Todd <sam.todd@latticeworks.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@latticeworks.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LatticeWorks — quick ask: real peak slope + latency SLOs

Stephanie — thanks, and great walkthrough. Quick answers: 

1) Traffic shape (observed last month):
- Baseline (off-peak): ~40 RPS across the service (chat+batch endpoints). Average tokens per request: 65 tokens.
- Peak hour (09:00–11:00 PT) hourly max: 720k requests (avg over the hour ~200 RPS).
- Concentration: we see 10-minute micro-peaks inside that hour. Conservatively assume 5x the hourly average for a 5–10 minute window (so ~1,000 RPS short spikes).
- For safety, include a weekend spike scenario where peak short-term RPS could reach 1,500 for special marketing pushes.

2) SLOs & fallback:
- Primary SLO: 95th-pct generation latency <= 400ms for the chat endpoint (typical prompt length ~65 tokens).
- Acceptable fallback: yes — degrade to an 7B quantized variant with slightly higher sampling latency if primary model is overloaded. We cannot tolerate >1s 95th-pct for chat during business hours.

Let me know if you need raw telemetry — we can share a 2-week debug window.

—Sam
Head of Platform, LatticeWorks

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Todd <sam.todd@latticeworks.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: first-pass slab simulation for LW-2345 (notes to review before we send to Sam)

Stephanie / Karthik — I ran the spreadsheet with Sam's numbers. High-level results (rounded):

Assumptions used:
- Chat model (primary): Redwood-13B-q4 (baseline perf measured on our fleet at 65 tokens/request): ~360 tokens/sec/GPU sustained at 95th-pct latency <=400ms with batching=dynamic and KV cache hit rate 60%.
- Fallback model: Redwood-7B-q4 with ~820 tokens/sec/GPU under same operating assumptions.
- Peak short-window RPS used for sizing: 1,000 RPS (Sam's 5x spike), tokens/request 65 -> required peak tokens/sec = 65,000 tokens/sec.

Sizing math (primary model):
- GPUs required (no buffer) = ceil(65,000 / 360) = 181 GPUs.
- Recommended safety multiplier for Dedicated deals = 1.25 (operational cushion + maintenance windows) -> 226 GPUs.
- Add 20% burst buffer for marketing campaigns -> final recommend slab = 271 GPUs.

With fallback enabled (automatic routing to 7B when latency breach imminent):
- Effective blended GPU need: primary slab sized for sustained baseline and small bursts (recommend 150 GPUs), plus a small on-demand burst pool sized to 121 GPUs (or 60 GPUs + dynamic hosted fallback) to meet 65k tokens/sec during 5–10 minute spikes. 

Notes: the absolute GPU counts are large because Sam's traffic assumptions imply a high tokens/sec concentration. We should propose a phased commit: initial 120-GPU Dedicated slab (to cover baseline + modest headroom) with a defined burst allocation and a 12-week runway to grow to 270 if traffic proves sticky. That reduces upfront cost and buys time to validate caching and prompt-level savings.

I attached the calculation PDF. Please check the operational notes — I called out opportunities to reduce GPUs by improving KV cache hit rate and increasing batching windows (lowers tokens/sec per GPU by up to ~20%).

-Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Steph Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Todd <sam.todd@latticeworks.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: first-pass slab simulation for LW-2345 (notes to review before we send to Sam)

Quick operational adjustments and recommended phrasing to Sam:

1) Break the ask into 2 proposals in the customer-facing note: "Conservative Dedicated Commitment" (phased up to 270 GPUs) and "Cost-optimized Commit" (initial 120 GPUs + aggressive cache + fallback SLA with hosted burst). That gives them optionality.

2) Call out measurable levers: improving KV cache hit from 60% -> 80% reduces required GPUs for primary model by ~17% (from 181 -> ~150 GPUs). Increasing average batching window by 30ms yields another ~8% improvement. Both are achievable with small SDK changes on their side.

3) For the billing/contract: recommend an explicit clause for marketing spikes (automatic 20% burst credit or short-term overage buckets) so they don't hit throttles unexpectedly.

I'll draft the customer-facing email. Laura, can you add a short SRE runbook for failover to quantized 7B (including traffic cutover steps and metrics to watch)?

-karthik

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sam Todd <sam.todd@latticeworks.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: LatticeWorks — Dedicated slab options and next steps (two proposals)

Sam — thanks for the data. Attached are two clear proposals so you can pick what fits your product risk profile: 

Option A — Conservative Dedicated Commitment (recommended if you need strong SLO headroom)
- Phase 1: 150 GPUs (Redwood-13B primary, expected to cover baseline and small bursts with ~18% headroom).
- Phase 2 (12 weeks): scale to 270 GPUs if observed 10-minute peak > 45k tokens/sec.
- Burst buffer: 20% automatic burst pool for 30-minute surge events.
- SLO guarantee: 95th-pct gen latency <= 400ms on primary; fallback to 7B quantized if breached.
- Pros: predictable tail performance, easier supportability.
- Cons: higher initial commit.

Option B — Cost-optimized commit (recommended if you want leaner upfront cost)
- Phase 1: 120 GPUs + hosted burst capacity for short spikes (~60 GPUs equivalent).
- Commitment term: 9 months with option to convert hosted bursts to Dedicated capacity after month 3.
- Requires engineering changes: KV cache improvements (target 80% hit) and batching tweaks (30ms batching window).
- Estimated steady-state cost: ~40% lower than Option A assuming KV/batching improvements.

Next steps: please confirm which option you'd like to explore and whether LatticeWorks can share a 2-week telemetry window so we can replace conservative multipliers with empirical numbers. Once we have that, we'll finalize the deal sizing and an SRE runbook (Laura will produce the failover doc).

Attachments: LW-2345_token_profile.xlsx, gpu_buffer_calc_v1.pdf, runbook_lattice_upload.docx

Best —
Stephanie
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
